clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991, within three years: your late nights began in autumn 1989 as the household shifted to Hollin Road with Desmond and his children; you dropped chess and debate; your mother filled in your college forms and you leaned hard on your closest friend Rafe once at conservatory in September 1991. Within weeks your wrist injury stopped your playing, you and Rafe clashed and he moved out, and you were on your own getting high and absorbed in radios through the winter. By early 1992 you were lost and low with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry. Your grandmother's thyroid surgery sat in these same months. Your functioning stayed down through a bleak year at community college before you found your drive again with an exchange to Lisbon in early 1994, stung that your father had never heard of your film; your shifts in these months are the reactions, and no one else's shifts show alongside yours through the end.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's death in February 2004, within three years: your anxiety climbed in autumn 2001 as you ran out of steam for performing, and your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002 alongside your disastrous audition. You grew distant from family and friends and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour in autumn 2002. You met Marisol that winter, moved to Fenwick with her by summer 2003, and split within the year. Once back in Thornbury that autumn you sank into depression, could not face your family, but relied on friends Corbin, Dale and Silas. You requested help with therapy costs and returned to your therapist Victor Halloran in January 2004, your functioning beginning to lift. Your last visit to your grandmother was brief and hung over on the way to the airport. Your shifts cluster around these months as you moved away and back, your functioning falling then slowly rising, your distance from family giving way to reaching toward your therapist and friends.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months before and after: you were too drained for conversation with your mother at Alder Creek in July 2008, she pressed to visit and you told her repeatedly the timing was wrong, but she drove out regardless and you kept the door shut on her. Within days you cut off from your mother entirely when you left for nursing school in August 2008, a silence that held for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke in January 2009 with months of rehabilitation ahead. These shifts in your relationship with your mother, your distance hardening into cutoff around the lodge visit, sit close together and alongside your grandmother's death the previous winter.

clusters.name: Wren joining the household, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within two years: you saw your mother less once Wren came along. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017. Your sister Tara had a baby on the way in autumn 2019. Your aunt Imogen's memory slipped worse and she lashed out when muddled. Your mother had a clear heart check-up after her siblings' illnesses. In October 2019 Wren was swamped with a street party, fundraising dinner and drive to the lake for her mother's retirement; you were too strict laying out a plan to settle her, she grew anxious when you had no sleep at family occasions, and long quiet drives home followed. Around the same time you felt you ought to be driving projects forward constantly, started a sleeping pill, and aimed for shorter regular calls with your mother. Your job steadied and paid well that June, yet your anxiety climbed again by October. These shifts in anxiety and functioning pile up across Wren's entry into your household and the press of her family's needs, while your extended family's illnesses multiply and your mother's contact with you eases.
